description: FEATURES-SCOPE PATTERN — "repeat THIS pocket" (pattern v2, docs/design/pattern-scope.md §8). A 40 x 40 x 20 plate, a 4 x 20 x 10 pocket at x in [4,8] extrude-CUT from the XY plane, then an 8 x 8 x 5 BOSS on the top face — a feature the user added for an unrelated reason — then a linear pattern (+X, spacing 12, count 3) with `scope: {kind: features, features: [pocket]}`. Three pockets at x in [4,8], [16,20], [28,32] and one boss: 29920.0 mm^3, bbox still 40 long. THIS TREE IS THE DEFECT'S OWN TREE. Delete the `scope` key and the identical tree evaluates to 51359.99999999999 with bbox X 0..64 — the boss SHADOWS the recorded cut, so v1's immediate-predecessor inference reads the request as "repeat the whole plate" and reports every feature `ok` (pattern-scope §1.1). What this golden locks is therefore not a new number but the removal of a guess: the seed is stated, so an unrelated feature between the cut and the pattern cannot change what is repeated. NOTE, and this is why the assertion set matters: the wrong body has the SAME face, edge and shell counts (26 / 60 / 1) as the right one. Topology alone does not catch it. Volume and the bounding box do.
derivation: Expectations are HAND-DERIVED analytic values, not recorded harness output (geometry-gates skill). All-planar throughout — no curved face anywhere, which is why the planar tolerance tier applies.
plate: x,y in [0,40] on XY (unconstrained -> the solver returns the authored positions bitwise), extruded 20 mm = 32000 mm^3.

pocket: a 4 x 20 rectangle at x in [4,8], y in [10,30], extrude-CUT 10 mm along +Z from the XY plane, so its tool spans z in [0,10] and the notch opens only at the z=0 face: -800 mm^3. This is the SAME notch the mirror-features goldens use, so its surface-area accounting is the reviewed one.

boss: an 8 x 8 square at x,y in [30,38] on a datum 20 mm above XY (the plate's top face), extruded 5 mm and fused: +320 mm^3. It is body-affecting and NOT a cut, so under the v1 body scope it shadows the pocket — that shadowing is the whole point of the fixture.

pattern, scope features [pocket], count 3 at spacing 12 along +X: the pocket's RECORDED removal tool is placed at +12 and +24 and cut, giving notches at x in [16,20] and x in [28,32]: -800 each. Both land inside the plate in plan, clear of one another (8 mm of material between consecutive notches) and clear of the boss (the notches span y in [10,30], the boss y in [30,38] and z >= 20), so the plate stays ONE connected solid and every removal is exact and independent.

surface_area: 6400 (the un-notched 40x40x20 plate = 2*1600 + 4*800) + 3 x 480 (each notch removes 80 mm^2 from the bottom cap and adds a 48 mm x 10 mm wall wrap plus an 80 mm^2 ceiling — the mirror-features goldens' reviewed per-notch figure) + 160 for the boss (-64 from the top cap, +4*40 of wall, +64 of new top) = 6400 + 1440 + 160 = 8000.0 mm^2.

bounding_box = [0,0,0]..[40,40,25]: every notch is interior in plan and opens downward; the boss adds the 5 mm above z=20. The X extent of 40 is the direct assertion that the PLATE was not replicated — the body reading of this same tree reaches 64.

topology: 26 faces = 6 outer + 5 per notch x 3 + 5 for the boss (4 walls + 1 top). 60 edges = 12 box + 12 per notch x 3 + 12 for the boss (4 of its footprint as an inner wire on the top cap, 4 vertical, 4 on its top). 1 shell.

mesh (linear 0.1 mm, all-planar): bottom cap = 4 outer + 3*4 notch nodes = 16 vertices with 3 holes -> 16 - 2 + 2*3 = 20 triangles. Top cap = 4 outer + 4 boss-footprint = 8 vertices with 1 hole -> 8 - 2 + 2 = 8 triangles. 4 plate side walls 16 / 8. Three notches at 5 faces each = 3*(20, 10) = 60 / 30. Boss = 4 walls (16 / 8) + 1 top (4 / 2) = 20 / 10. Totals = 16 + 8 + 16 + 60 + 20 = 120 vertices and 20 + 8 + 8 + 30 + 10 = 76 triangles.
GLB byte size is deliberately NOT pinned (as in every sibling golden); the determinism leg of the runner already asserts byte-identical GLB across rebuilds and across a fresh interpreter.
tolerance_rationale: ALL-PLANAR tolerance — the same reviewed planar tier as the mirror-features goldens and the shipped planar pattern goldens; reused verbatim, no new epsilon. Measured deviations vs the analytic values (2026-08-26, build123d 0.11.1 / OCCT 7.9): volume |29920.0 - 29920.000000000004| = 3.6e-12, surface_area 9.1e-13, centroid.x exactly 0.0, centroid.y exactly 0.0, centroid.z 8.9e-15, AABB bounds exactly 0.0. ~275x headroom over the worst residual. Topology and mesh counts carry NO tolerance (exact-match) — and per the description they are NOT what discriminates this golden's body from the defect's body, so a future change that keeps them and moves the volume is exactly what this file exists to catch. Loosening requires a reviewed kernel-level justification recorded here and in docs/GEOMETRY-QA.md.
